0.0.n: A very casual word for oneself, typically used by men.

0.1.n: After 俺, this stresses that the speaker shares the same desire as others.

0.2.n: The stem of 遊ぶ pairs with に and a movement verb to express the purpose of going.

0.3.n: Marks 遊び as the purpose of going, rather than a destination.

0.4.n: 行く becomes 行きたい with たい, expressing the speaker’s desire.

0.5.n: A casual, forceful sentence ending with a typically masculine feel.

1.0.n: Introduces a contrast with the wish expressed in the previous line.

1.1.n: Names the present moment, contrasted here with when going out might be possible.

1.2.n: Makes 今 the topic, emphasizing what applies right now.

1.3.n: A noun used here to urge holding back from going out.

1.4.n: The plain form of です makes the statement direct and firm.

2.0.n: Together with で, this includes everyone in the proposed action.

2.1.n: After みんな, this marks the group acting jointly.

2.2.n: Points to the crisis shared by the speaker and listeners; it must come before a noun.

2.3.n: Refers to the difficult situation that everyone is being urged to overcome.

2.4.n: Marks 危機 as what the group will overcome.

2.5.n: 乗り越える becomes 乗り越えよう, a form used to propose a shared action.

2.6.n: Adds energetic, casual encouragement to the invitation, with a typically masculine feel.

3.0.n: An English phrase borrowed into Japanese and used here as a slogan.

3.2.n: The prefix お gives うち a warm, familiar tone here.

3.3.n: Marks home as the location where the proposed activity happens.

3.4.n: 過ごす becomes 過ごそう, inviting the listeners to join the speaker in an action.

0.lit: I too, for having fun, want to go!
0.tip: A verb stem plus に行く means going to do something; たい adds the desire to go.

1.lit: But as for now, it is restraint!
1.tip: 我慢だ is a compact way to say it is time to hold back or endure.

2.lit: Everyone together, this crisis, let’s overcome!
2.tip: The ending よう in 乗り越えよう turns the verb into an invitation: let’s overcome it.

3.lit: Stay home! At home, let’s spend time!
3.tip: で marks where an action happens, so おうちで tells us where to spend time.
